description: Surveys — taking a survey the back end holds and recording one response to it. Two styles: ranked choice (the options chosen in priority order, plus one write-in that was not in the set) and rating scales (Likert, frequency, satisfaction, NPS, stars, semantic differentials, with opt-outs and a comment). A program names the survey with `id "…"`; what it asks, its scales and its bounds come from the survey itself and CANNOT be written in code. A survey with several versions draws one per session. L0182 describes no flow and has no interactive player.

example_prompts.prompt: Answer the civic-priorities survey for me — I pick whichever two options you think matter most.
example_prompts.notes: The ordinary request: a survey exists and what is brought to it is an answer. `survey [id "civic-priorities" session-id get-val-public "itemId" response [...]]` — the options come back from the survey, and the program never writes them.

example_prompts.prompt: Answer the team-retro survey with cutting the build time in half first, then the flaky tests.
example_prompts.notes: `choices` names the options chosen and the order IS the ranking. Name each by its exact text — the options live in the survey, so the ids cannot be known when the response is written.

example_prompts.prompt: Add my own option alongside my choices: make public transit free.
example_prompts.notes: `write-in` must not repeat one already in the set — that is what makes it new.

example_prompts.prompt: Record just a new option — I do not want to pick any of the existing ones.
example_prompts.notes: `write-in` may stand alone; `choices` comes back empty, where the survey's floor allows it.

example_prompts.prompt: Reorder my selection so the housing option comes first.
example_prompts.notes: Reordering `choices` IS re-ranking; there is no separate rank step.

example_prompts.prompt: Fill in the course-feedback survey: agree with every statement except the pace, and I'd give it a 9 for recommending it.
example_prompts.notes: A rating survey. `response [ratings [[item "…" rating "Agree"] … [item "…" rating 9]]]` — each item named by its text, each rating a label on its scale or the scale's own value. 9 on a 0–10 scale is 9, never a position.

example_prompts.prompt: Rate the app-usability survey as someone using the app for the first time.
example_prompts.notes: A semantic differential: each item sits on a 1–7 scale between its own two words, and `rating` may be a number or one of those end words.

example_prompts.prompt: Mark the lab question not applicable and add a comment that the labs were rushed.
example_prompts.notes: An opt-out is the scale's own words ("Not applicable") and is recorded as an opt-out, not a value. `comment` is accepted only where the survey asks for one.

Ranked choice: civic-priorities, team-retro, city-budget, product-features and school. Rating: course-feedback, customer-satisfaction, app-usability and workplace-pulse. An id that does not exist is a compile error naming the ones that do.

example_prompts.prompt: Take version 7 of civic-priorities rather than whichever one it gives me.
example_prompts.notes: `id "civic-priorities-7"` takes that version outright, with no draw. The version drawn for a session is in `instance` in the compiled record.

example_prompts.prompt: Set up a survey asking my team what to fix first, with these eight options.
example_prompts.notes: NOT possible here. A survey's options or items, scales, wording and bounds belong to the back end, and no word writes them; L0182 only takes surveys that already exist.
